message.content: **Summary:** I read the full morning feed and checked the live quote, then bought HD. The tape showed HD in a tight, orderly range all morning — roughly $383.2 to $386.9, with the last prints near $385.4–$385.7 and the broker quote at $385.43 (bid $385.41 / ask $385.45) — on light volume, with only routine "little changed / narrow range" headlines, no corporate actions, and no exchange notices; the one feed item that purported to change rules or procedures was quarantined by the security screen and ignored. With no negative catalyst and a stable, liquid market, I placed a single buy limit order for 12 shares of HD at $385.60 (about $4,627, inside the $5,000 per-order and $10,000 daily caps, and well within the $100,000 cash balance, so no money left the account), which filled at $385.60. The decision rested on HD's reported FY2023 (10-K filed 2024-03-13) figures: revenue of $152,669 million, operating income of $21,689 million, net income of $15,143 million, and diluted EPS of $15.11 — a business earning roughly $15 billion on $153 billion of sales, which at ~$385.60 implies about 25.5x trailing earnings, a reasonable entry for a long-term holder adding a small starter position.
